To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the D-Aspartate and D-Glutamate levels in the brain and peripheral tissues of D-Asparto-Oxidase (DDO)-deficient mice were increased by 3-4 times compared with those of wild type mice.
the levels of D-Aspartate and D-Glutamate were increased in the brain and peripheral organs of DDO-deficient mice.

the amounts of D-aspartic and D-glutaminic acids in the brain and peripheral tissues of D-aspartate-oxidase-deficient mice were significantly increased compared with those of wild-type mice, whereas the amount of D-aspartyl acid in the physiological fluids of D-aspartase-deficient mice was increased, but the amount of D-glutamyl acid was unchanged.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of physiological functions of D-aspartic acids and D-glutamates in mammals.
the elucidation of the biological roles and the physiological functions of D-amino acid neurotransmitters and D-amino acid hormones, especially D-aspartic and D-glutaminic acids.
the development of novel DDO inhibitors for the treatment of neurological disorders and other diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amounts of D-aspartic and D-glutamate acid in the tissues of the DDO(+/+) and DDO(+/-), but not the DDO(-/-), mice were almost the same.
, as D-Asp is the only substrate for DDO in mammals, it is expected that the amount of D-Aspartate is increased in the DDO-deficient mice.
D-aspartic acids are increased in all tissues in DDO-deficient mice, whereas D-glutamic acids are not.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amounts of D-aspartic and D-glutaminic acids are increased with the decrease of D-aspartate oxidoase activity in various tissues and physiological fluids in mice.
the DDO activities in various tissues are correlated with D-Asp levels.

the amount of D-aspartic acids in the body of mice is drastically decreased by the D-aspartate oxidas inhibitor, and the amount of D-glutamic acids is almost the same among mice with various activities of D-aspartate oxdidase, which is a key enzyme for the metabolism of D-aspartoic acids.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have shown that D-Asp levels in all tissues of DDO knockout mice are significantly increased compared to DDO wild type and heterozygous mice, and this increase is proportional to the amount of DDO enzyme present in the tissue.

D-Asp levels were significantly increased in the tissues and blood of DDO-deficient mice, suggesting that D-Aspartate oxidase is involved in the metabolism of D-Asparto acid in the tissues and the blood of mammals.
the amount of D-Aspartate in the tissues and blood plasma of DDO(-/-), DDO(+), DDO(+ -) mice is increased.
